items.question: How does the triadic world-manifestation arise from consciousness?
premises: The abiding state takes the form of knower, known, and knowing.
This state belongs to perfectly full own-consciousness.
The fashioning of the manifold world occurs spontaneously from that consciousness.
items.inference: The entire triadic manifestation is the spontaneous, constant self-expression of perfectly full consciousness.
items.plain_english: Such an abiding state, having the form of knower, known, and knowing, is always the spontaneous fashioning of the manifold world by perfectly full own-consciousness.

rows.grounds: compound expressing total pervasion of consciousness
the capacity to discern reality and unreality
points to consciousness as the source

items.question: From what source does the determination of truth and falsity arise?
premises: Own-consciousness intrinsically takes the form of all beings, directions, places, and times.
The determination of truth and falsity is a cognitive act.
That determination arises from consciousness alone.
items.inference: Because consciousness pervades all forms, it alone is the source of discerning truth from falsity.
items.plain_english: She indeed is by herself the form of all, of all selves, directions, places, and times; and from her alone arises the determination of what is true and what is false.

rows.grounds: adds this authority to the argument
describes the ambiguous status of external objects
locates the true ground of appearance
identifies perception as rooted in self-awareness

items.question: What did Utpaladeva teach about the status of external objects?
premises: Teacher Utpaladeva also taught this very point.
What appears outside may seem to be being or nonbeing.
Such appearance is grounded in own-consciousness as my seeing.
items.inference: Even the seemingly external world of being and nonbeing is established within own-consciousness.
items.plain_english: Teacher Utpaladeva also taught this very thing: even what appears outside as being or nonbeing is, in own-consciousness, my seeing.

rows.grounds: imperative expressing the freedom of consciousness
the self-imposed order of the free
names this regulation as inclusive of the senses
the self-awareness that is rested upon

items.question: How does the autonomous consciousness regulate itself across all beings?
premises: The principle 'let it see' expresses the regulation of the autonomous.
This regulation, called together with the senses, pervades from Shiva down to the worm.
Throughout this range it rests upon its own consciousness.
items.inference: The same autonomous self-awareness regulates and pervades all levels of existence from highest to lowest.
items.plain_english: The regulation of the autonomous, expressed as 'let it see' and called together with the senses, is that very consciousness which, ascending from Shiva down to the worm, rests upon its own awareness.

rows.grounds: locates the state in the divine
one who has reached that rest

items.question: What distinguishes bondage from liberation in relation to consciousness?
premises: The same reality is worldly bondage in the limited condition and Shiva the supreme lord in truth.
Attaining rest in that consciousness changes one's condition.
One who has attained rest there is called liberated.
items.inference: Bondage and liberation are not different realities but different relations to the same supreme consciousness.
items.plain_english: That very same reality is worldly bondage, and it is Shiva, the supreme lord; one who has attained rest in it is called liberated.

rows.grounds: states the dependence of all beings
includes the lowest forms of existence
points to the consciousness under discussion

items.question: What sustains all beings from Brahma down to the immobile?
premises: All beings from Brahma to the immobile live by the grace of this consciousness.
This consciousness is always unobscured.
It should therefore be recognized as the sustaining reality.
items.inference: The ever-unobscured consciousness is the universal life-giving ground of all beings.
items.plain_english: By the grace of this, all beings from Brahma down to the immobile live; let this consciousness be understood as always unobscured.

rows.grounds: names consciousness in its divine aspect
the self that is established or altered

items.question: Does the shining goddess ever become separate from herself in her operations?
premises: The goddess shines forth everywhere.
She may establish the self in one place and fault it in another.
Nowhere is anything devoid of her.
items.inference: Even while performing diverse operations, the goddess never becomes separate from herself.
items.plain_english: Even while shining forth, that goddess never establishes a self anywhere as devoid of her; in one place she may establish it, in another fault it, in another do otherwise.

rows.grounds: compound stating she is untouched by her own operations
names consciousness in its sovereign aspect

items.question: Do the goddess's acts of establishing and faulting alter her own nature?
premises: The goddess places things in various ways.
She does not undergo change.
She remains untouched by establishing, faulting, and otherness.
items.inference: The supreme goddess performs diverse operations without any alteration to her own nature.
items.plain_english: She places things otherwise, yet she does not undergo change; even while barren of establishing, faulting, and otherness, she remains the supreme goddess.

rows.grounds: refers to prior teachers or beings

items.question: Who is the primordial teacher behind this autonomous shining of consciousness?
premises: The goddess shines clearly in that very autonomous way.
The glorious great lord is the teacher even of earlier teachers.
This lord is identified with that autonomous consciousness.
items.inference: The autonomous, clearly shining consciousness is the glorious great lord, the primordial teacher of all.
items.plain_english: And she shines clearly in that very way, autonomous indeed; she is the glorious great lord, the god who is the teacher even of those who came before.

rows.grounds: the true ground to be honored

items.question: What teaching did the great lord proclaim for the grace of the world?
premises: The great lord proclaimed this teaching out of grace for the world.
He criticized abiding in essenceless speech like the cawing of crows.
Those who honor their own consciousness and the instruction of the goddess-consciousness become liberated while living.
items.inference: Turning to one's own consciousness and heeding its immediate instruction leads to living liberation in any place.
uncertainties: sarva appears as a stem form where sarve might be expected; taken as m.nom.pl in context.
items.plain_english: He proclaimed this for the grace of the world: 'Deluded ones, why do you abide in vain in essenceless speech like the cawing of crows? Honoring your own consciousness, all who respect what is instructed even nearby by the goddess-consciousness become liberated while living, in whatever place they are.'

rows.grounds: the modes by which it swallows the universe

items.question: Why is consciousness itself called the true teacher in this doctrine?
premises: In this guiding principle, consciousness alone is called the teacher.
The teacher is so called because it swallows the universe.
It swallows the universe through the processes of creation and dissolution.
items.inference: Consciousness is the true guru because it emits and reabsorbs the entire universe.
items.plain_english: Therefore, in this guiding principle, consciousness alone is called the teacher, because it indeed swallows the universe through creation and dissolution.

items.question: What makes a relation with the teacher the supreme one?
premises: The primary, firm relation is called the supreme relation.
Through that relation, whatever is instructed becomes knowledge.
That knowledge is innately accomplished.
items.inference: The supreme relation to the teacher is the one through which instruction immediately becomes innately perfected knowledge.
items.plain_english: Therefore, here the primary firm relation is called the supreme one; whatever knowledge is instructed through it is indeed innately accomplished.

rows.grounds: the unchanging condition of the lineage
indicates the source of the lineage
describes the unfolding of the tradition

items.question: From what abiding ground does the Tryambaka lineage proceed?
premises: Our lineage of teachers has an eternal abiding.
The division of the lineage beginning with Tryambaka proceeds from that abiding.
That abiding is the source of the tradition's continuity.
items.inference: The Tryambaka transmission stream proceeds from the eternal abiding of the teachers' lineage in consciousness.
items.plain_english: Where the eternal abiding of our lineage of teachers is established, from there proceeds the division of the transmission beginning with Tryambaka.

rows.grounds: the mistaken identification to be removed

items.question: How does the world appear once identity with ignorance perishes?
premises: It was said earlier that identity with ignorance perishes.
Own-consciousness takes on variety.
This world shines forth from that variety of own-consciousness.
items.inference: When ignorance dissolves, the world is seen to shine as the varied display of own-consciousness.
items.plain_english: Where it was previously said that identity with ignorance perishes, this world shines forth from the variety grasped by own-consciousness.

rows.grounds: classifies levels of scriptures or beings
describes teachings as rays of true speech
created by the teacher's own being

items.question: How should the diverse levels of scripture be understood in relation to the teacher?
premises: Scriptures range through intermediate, great-divine, divine, and other levels.
These teachings are rays of the teacher's own true speech.
They are fashioned by the teacher's own self.
items.inference: The confluence of diverse scriptures consists of self-fashioned rays of the teacher's own true speech.
uncertainties: The compound antarālamahaddivyādivyādi is compressed; the exact class boundaries follow the tradition's scriptural taxonomy.
items.plain_english: The confluence of scriptures—intermediate, great-divine, divine, and so forth—consists of the rays of the teacher's own true speech, fashioned by his own self.

items.question: Why is the present effort focused primarily on own-consciousness?
premises: The primacy of own-consciousness is manifest.
Authority may be traced to the teacher, scripture, or oneself.
This effort is made with own-consciousness as primary.
items.inference: Because own-consciousness is manifestly primary, the exposition rightly focuses its main effort on it.
items.plain_english: The primacy of own-consciousness is manifest—whether from the teacher, from scripture, or from oneself; therefore this effort has been made with that as primary.

rows.grounds: describes the teacher's reliance on scripture

items.question: How do teacher, scripture, and self-consciousness relate in producing realization?
premises: The teacher depends on the operation of scripture.
Scripture is established in one's own self-consciousness.
All of this attains accomplishment through self-consciousness and is never obstructed.
items.inference: Teacher and scripture are effective only because they are grounded in self-consciousness, which unfailingly accomplishes realization.
uncertainties: asahyatām is read as 'unbearableness' in the sense of not being able to be withstood or obstructed; the nuance is slightly compressed.
items.plain_english: The teacher depends on the operation of scripture, and that is established in one's own self-consciousness; therefore all this attains accomplishment through self-consciousness and is never obstructed.

items.question: How should seekers of liberation direct their study and effort?
premises: This scripture should be practiced with effort.
Seekers of liberation are the intended audience.
Life should not be wasted in strained effort over other scriptures.
items.inference: Seekers of liberation should devote their effort to practicing this scripture rather than dispersing life in other teachings.
items.plain_english: O seekers of liberation, let this scripture be practiced with effort; do not let life be spent in vain, strained over other scriptures.

rows.grounds: states where both views are resolved

items.question: How does this teaching relate to views of difference and non-difference?
premises: There are views of non-difference and views of difference.
Both kinds of views come to fulfillment here alone.
Therefore this teaching deserves careful examination.
items.inference: Because both dualist and nondualist views find their fulfillment in this teaching, it should be thoroughly examined.
items.plain_english: Whatever view of non-difference or view of difference there may be, it comes to fulfillment here alone; therefore let this be carefully examined.

items.question: What is the effect of sustained practice of this scripture?
premises: One who recognizes the dream state becomes freed from sleep.
Practice of this scripture awakens the heart.
The awakened state becomes constant.
items.inference: Sustained practice of this scripture awakens the heart permanently, like recognizing a dream and waking from sleep.
items.plain_english: Just as one is freed from sleep by recognizing the dream state, so one whose heart is awakened by sustained practice of this scripture remains always awake.

rows.grounds: the teaching in its deepest sense

items.question: What is the ultimate source of the scripture's authority?
premises: Own-consciousness is that very scripture.
Own-consciousness is free from dependence on anything else.
If self-derived authoritativeness is to be affirmed, it belongs to own-consciousness.
items.inference: The scripture's ultimate authority is the self-valid, independent authority of own-consciousness itself.
items.plain_english: Own-consciousness indeed is that scripture, and she is free from dependence; if it is to be stated thus, let its authoritativeness be said to be from itself.

rows.grounds: the act or content of instruction

items.question: How are teaching, teacher, and taught unified in the highest state?
premises: Teaching, what is to be taught, and the teacher form a triad.
In the highest state this triad is not measured by time.
That state is beautiful with freedom and nonduality.
items.inference: In the timeless supreme state, the triad of teaching, taught, and teacher is unified in the beauty of freedom and nonduality.
uncertainties: tattatrākālakalitaṃ is a dense compound; the reading follows the sense of being beyond temporal division in that state.
items.plain_english: Teaching, what is to be taught, and the teacher—this triad, in that state, is not measured by time and is beautiful with freedom and nonduality.

items.question: Where did Shrikantha proclaim this intrinsic, never-departing state?
premises: There is an intrinsic state that never departs.
This state can be internalized.
Lord Shrikantha proclaimed it in the glorious Kirana scripture.
items.inference: The intrinsic, never-departing state of consciousness was authoritatively proclaimed by Shrikantha in the Kirana scripture.
items.plain_english: Having internalized that intrinsic, never-departing state, lord Shrikantha proclaimed it in the glorious Kirana scripture.

items.question: Why does the teaching appear divided if its ultimate state is nondual?
premises: All this teaching is presented for the engagement of hearers.
It is differentiated according to differences of meaning.
This difference is constructed by metaphorical usage.
items.inference: The apparent divisions in the teaching are provisional, pedagogical constructions rather than ultimate differences.
uncertainties: The token 'śrot\rr' contains a backslash-r sequence as given in the source; it appears to be part of the transmitted form of śrotṝṇām split across tokens and is preserved exactly.
items.plain_english: All this is for the sake of engaging hearers through differentiation; but this difference, arising from difference of meaning, is constructed only by metaphorical usage.
